hook: Where Jane Austen Wrote Her Novels
text: Jane Austen never had a study of her own. At the cottage in Chawton, she wrote in the family sitting room, at a small table by the window, hardly bigger than a tea tray. According to her nephew's memoir, she wrote on small sheets of paper that could be slipped away or covered if a visitor came in. And the family remembered a door that creaked whenever it opened. She asked them not to fix it, so the story goes, because the creak warned her that someone was coming. At that little table, she revised or wrote all six of her novels.
